decision: Should TensorLBM adopt the OSS raster-obstacle operator of ebinan92/Fingering_dynamics (hand-written 8-class corner-class bounce-back tables, bounce_back.py:25-86) as its raster-obstacle wall treatment, or keep its per-direction closed-link mask (bitflag_neighbour_mask) as the production path? Decision criterion = physical observable disagreement between the two operators on identical raster geometry.
alternatives: A (OSS / reference arm): corner-class half-way bounce-back table painted from each rectangle's bounding box (N/S/E/W bands + 4 diagonal corner cells), periodic np.roll streaming, wall rows by bottom_top_wall.
B (TensorLBM / got arm): exact per-direction closed-link bitmask (bit i-1 set iff x-c_i is solid) driving stream+bounce-back; corner classes emerge from the bit pattern instead of being painted.
hypothesis: H1: the OSS corner-class table and the exact closed-link mask differ only on the diagonal links at the ends of each N/S/E/W band (8 links per isolated rectangle), so any physical observable (permeability, obstacle drag) differs by less than the owner 15% bar. H0: the difference is material (>=15%) somewhere on the ladder.

metrics.K_oss: lattice permeability of this arm: K = nu * u_bar / g, u_bar = pore mean of u_x
metrics.fx: momentum-exchange force on the obstacles, F_x = sum over the arm's bounced obstacle links of 2 c_ix f_opp (pre-stream populations)
metrics.field_rel_l2: ||u_x(mask) - u_x(oss)||_2 / ||u_x(oss)||_2 over fluid nodes, per cent
metrics.spurious_links: count of links bounced by the OSS table whose upstream cell is fluid
metrics.missed_links: count of exact solid links not bounced by the OSS table
metrics.anchor_err_pct: C0 (no obstacles) |K_sim - K_analytic| / K_analytic, K_analytic = ny^2/12 + 1/24

predeclared_thresholds.operator_equivalence_rule: every exact solid link must be in the OSS table set (missed_links = 0); the table may add links, each of which must be classified and counted
predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: stop when max|u(t) - u(t-check_every)| / |u_bar| < u_rel_tol, capped at the predeclared step budget; no run extended or truncated after inspecting K
predeclared_thresholds.failure_rule: non-finite fields or non-convergence inside the budget are reported as FAILED / NOT_CONVERGED, never re-tuned

unit_of_analysis: one steady-state 2-D LBM run (one config x one arm); the metric unit is one geometry/parameter point

baseline_control.baseline: OSS arm (C1) = the reference implementation of the anchor tag
baseline_control.control_no_obstacle: C0: no obstacles; both arms must reproduce the discrete Poiseuille permeability ny^2/12 + 1/24 within 3 % -- proves the collision/forcing/measurement chain is sound before any obstacle difference is interpreted
baseline_control.control_same_collision: both arms share the identical BGK collision, Guo forcing, seed field and measurement code; the only changed variable is the bounce-back link set
baseline_control.geometry_control: both arms read the same raster mask built from the same rectangle corner list; solid fraction, block count and mask equality are recorded

variables_changed: bounce-back operator (corner-class table vs exact closed-link mask)
lattice resolution: block edge b = 12 (132x144) vs b = 24 (264x288), identical porosity and block count
variables_controlled: raster geometry (same rect corner list, same solid mask, 12 blocks, 9.09 % solid)
seed field, time-step budget, convergence tolerance, measurement code
single-phase D2Q9 BGK, Guo second-order body force, double precision numpy
confounders: the OSS arm in the reference repo is coupled to a non-Newtonian free-energy solver; here only its bounce-back operator (with its own streaming and wall routine) is transplanted onto a single-phase BGK stepper, so the measured difference isolates the operator, not the phase field

the OSS main run uses the two end x-columns as Zou-He inlet/outlet and applies bottom_top_wall only to the interior columns; here the domain is periodic in x and the wall routine is applied to every column (documented porting deviation)
K is a volume-averaged scalar; two operators can give the same K with different local fields, so the field L2 difference is reported alongside
the spurious links are a geometric artefact of the band painting, so their effect scales with block perimeter / porosity rather than with Re; the ladder varies resolution and forcing to show this
repetition_rationale: the integrations are deterministic (no randomness, no seeds beyond the deterministic initial field), so repetition is not used for uncertainty; instead the ladder varies tau, g and resolution (5 points) to show that the arm difference is not an accident of one parameter point

environment.layout: float64, CPU numpy, (9, nx, ny) with D2Q9_C ordering 1=E,2=N,3=W,4=S,5=NE,6=NW,7=SW,8=SE
environment.cluster: 702 two-node loong64 (128 cores each), jobs submitted through the platform cluster queue, nodes assigned by the scheduler
environment.resource_limit: each shard <= 1800 s wall; total ladder 6 configs x 2 arms

analysis_plan: for every config: K per arm, err_k_pct, fx per arm, err_fx_pct, field L2; accept when err_k_pct < 15 %. Additionally classify the operator difference link by link (spurious / missed) and report the analytic anchor error. Aggregation is a straight table, no outlier removal, no post-hoc threshold changes.
stopping_rule: the ladder is fixed in advance (C0..C5); no config is added after seeing results, and a config is reported as NOT_CONVERGED rather than re-run with a longer budget
interpretation_limits: the comparison is operator-level: it says whether transplanting the OSS corner-class table would change TensorLBM's raster-obstacle physics by more than 15 % on this geometry family. It does not measure the OSS free-energy/wetting physics, which was XVAL'd separately (XVAL-LBM-DIFFUSE-INTERFACE-WETTING-VIA-WALL-ORDER-PARAMETER) and which produced no usable OSS number.
